newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israeli foreign minister to visit Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Israeli foreign minister to visit Jordan.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy will visit Jordan on Thursday for talks on relations frayed by Israel's encouragement of Jewish settlement in the West Bank.
An Israeli embassy official said on Monday Levy would meet Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti.
His visit follows a trip to Israel last week by Jordan's Information Minister Marwan Muasher.

Muasher told journalists after a cabinet meeting on Sunday that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's encouragement of Jewish settlement in occupied Arab land "posed a direct threat to the (Middle East) peace process".
"The Israeli policies tend to revive the idea of a substitute homeland (for Palestinians) and in the final analysis these settlements directly threaten Jordan," he said.
Jordan's official Petra news agency said Netanyahu called King Hussein on Monday to assure him that Israel "was continuing its diligent work to push forward negotiations" with Palestinians.
Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994, ending a 46-year state of war.

Levy is also expected to inaugurate a new embassy building in Amman during his visit. Israeli diplomats have been operating from offices in a five-star hotel since they opened their mission to Jordan in December 1994.
